english.goal: I can describe a character from what they do, use commas in a list, and use sounds to read new words.

learn.title: The collector
learn.text: In the poem Younger Brother, the boy collects lots of things: feathers, stones, seeds and badges. Someone who collects things is called a collector.

learn.title: Actions show character
learn.text: What a character does tells us what they are like. He collects lots of unusual things, so he is curious. He keeps socks under the bed, so he is messy!

learn.title: Commas in a list
learn.text: When we list 3 or more things, we put a comma between them. Before the last thing we write and. There is no comma before and.
learn.big: I collect shells, stickers, keys and coins.

learn.title: Sound it out
learn.text: To read a new word: look at it, spot a sound you know, say each sound, then blend them together. Don't guess!
learn.extra: Sounds to spot: sh · ai · ay · ee · igh

learn.title: This week's spellings
learn.text: Look at the word. Say it. Cover it. Write it. Check it!

maths.goal: I can name and sort 2D and 3D shapes, describe them, and spot shapes that are symmetrical.

learn.title: 2D shapes are flat
learn.text: 2D shapes are flat, like a drawing on paper. We describe them by counting their sides and corners. A corner is called a vertex.

learn.title: 3D shapes are solid
learn.text: 3D shapes are solid. You can hold them in your hand, like a ball or a box!

learn.title: Faces, edges and vertices
learn.text: A face is a flat side. An edge is where two faces meet. A vertex is a corner. A cube has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices.

learn.title: Curved or flat?
learn.text: A sphere, cylinder and cone have a curved surface, so they can roll! A cube, cuboid and pyramid have only flat faces.

learn.title: Symmetry
learn.text: A shape is symmetrical when a line splits it into two halves that match exactly, like a mirror. Many buildings in the UAE are symmetrical too!

gp.goal: I can say what a country is and compare large and small countries. I can talk about where our food comes from.

learn.title: What is a country?
learn.text: A country is an area of land with borders around it. Each country has its own name, flag, leaders and rules. There are nearly 200 countries in the world!

learn.title: Big and small countries
learn.text: Countries come in all sizes. Canada is huge and has thousands of lakes. Vatican City is the smallest country in the world, smaller than a big park!
learn.big: Canada → very big   ·   Vatican City → tiny

learn.title: Our country
learn.text: We live in the UAE, a country in Asia. It sits next to the sparkling Arabian Gulf.

learn.title: Where does our food come from?
learn.text: Some food grows on plants, like dates, rice and tomatoes. Some comes from animals, like milk, eggs and fish. Local food is grown near where we live, like UAE dates!

items.t: Countries can be found on maps
Every country has its own flag
All countries are the same size
A country is a kind of ocean

items.q: What shows where one country stops and another starts?

msc.goal: I can describe my family and explain how family members help each other.

learn.title: What is a family?
learn.text: A family is a group of people who care for each other and help each other. Some families are big and some are small. Every family is special.

learn.title: Family words
learn.text: Families can have mums, dads, brothers, sisters, grandparents, aunts, uncles, cousins, and even pets!

learn.title: Everyone helps
learn.text: In a family, everyone can help. Grown-ups cook and drive. Children can tidy toys, water plants, feed a pet or play with a baby.

learn.title: Families in the UAE
learn.text: Many families in the UAE meet at their grandparents' home for Friday lunch. On Eid and National Day, families and neighbours share food and help each other.

practice.title: Ali's family
practice.text:
Ali is seven and lives in Dubai. He lives with his mum, his dad, his big brother Khaled, his baby sister Hamda, his grandma, his grandpa and his cat, Lulu.
Everyone in Ali's family helps. Khaled tidies the bedroom. Mum cooks dinner and Grandma looks after baby Hamda. Grandpa works in the garden. Dad helps with homework and cooks at the weekend.
Ali helps too! He plays with Hamda and cleans Lulu's bed and toys.
practice.prompt: Tap 5 people (or pets!) in Ali's family.
